HOUSING COOPERATIVE LIPOVÁ 12-18 - BOARD MEETING MINUTES
Meeting no. 3/2026, held on 18 March 2026 at 18:30 in the community room, building 14
Board members present: K. Novotná (chair), P. Dvořák (technical committee), H. Králová (treasurer), T. Beneš (facilities manager), J. Svoboda, M. Říhová, L. Procházka, O. Němec, V. Fialová
Guests: 14 cooperative members; Ing. R. Horák (energy auditor) for item 3

1. Opening

The chair opened the meeting at 18:32 and confirmed that all nine board members were present, so the board can adopt resolutions by a simple majority (5 votes). The chair reminded guests that they may speak to each item but do not vote, and that a proposal is adopted only when the board passes it by a vote recorded in these minutes. Proposals that are discussed but not voted, or voted down, are recorded for information only.

2. Approval of the previous minutes

The minutes of meeting no. 2/2026 were approved (9 for). The chair noted one correction requested by Mr. Němec: the quote for the roof inspection mentioned in those minutes was EUR 1,900, not EUR 1,600.

2b. Reports

The caretaker reported on the winter season: snow clearing was needed on 11 days, two burst pipes in the basement of building 12 were repaired under the insurance policy, and the main entrance door of building 14 was replaced after the closing mechanism failed. The treasurer presented the 2025 accounts: income from member contributions EUR 186,400, operating expenses EUR 151,900, and a transfer of EUR 30,000 to the repair fund, which now stands at EUR 162,000. Members asked about arrears; three flats are more than two months in arrears and have received a written reminder. The auditor's report is expected in April. The board took note of the reports without a vote, as they require no resolution.

The chair reported on correspondence: the town has announced that the street in front of buildings 16 and 18 will be closed for sewer works for four weeks in June, and the gas distribution company will replace the meters in all buildings during the summer.

3. Energy renovation package

Ing. Horák presented the energy audit of buildings 12 to 18 completed in February. The audit identified four measures: (a) external thermal insulation of the facades, (b) replacement of the gas boilers with air-to-water heat pumps, (c) photovoltaic panels on the roofs of buildings 14 and 16, and (d) balancing of the heating system. He estimated that measures (a) and (d) together would reduce heating energy use by about 31%, and that (b) would cut emissions further but at a much higher capital cost. Members asked about noise from heat pumps and about the subsidy schedule; Ing. Horák answered that the national subsidy programme reopens in September.

3a. Facade insulation

Mr. Dvořák, for the technical committee, presented the proposal to insulate the facades of all four buildings with 160 mm mineral wool, as recommended in the audit. The proposal as circulated on 4 March carried a budget of EUR 230,000. After the technical committee obtained a second quote that excluded the scaffolding of building 18 (which is already scaffolded for the balcony repairs), Mr. Dvořák moved an amendment reducing the budget to EUR 214,000. The amendment was accepted by the board (8 for, 1 abstention).

Resolution 3/2026-1: The board ADOPTS the facade insulation of buildings 12-18 with a budget of EUR 214,000, to be managed by the technical committee under Mr. P. Dvořák. Works start on 1 May 2026. Vote: 9 for. Adopted.

3b. Heat pumps

Mr. Svoboda moved that the cooperative replace the gas boilers with heat pumps in the same works season. Several members supported the proposal; others pointed out that the cooperative's reserve fund would not cover both the insulation and the heat pumps without a loan, and that the subsidy should be applied for first. Mr. Procházka noted that installing heat pumps before the facades are insulated would oversize them.

The proposal to install heat pumps was put to the vote: 4 for, 5 against. The heat pump proposal was NOT adopted. The board asked the technical committee to bring a revised proposal, with a subsidy application and a financing plan, to the autumn meeting.

[page 2]
3c. Photovoltaic panels

Ms. Říhová presented an offer for photovoltaic panels on the roofs of buildings 14 and 16. The board agreed that the roof inspection must be completed first. The item was deferred to the next meeting without a vote. No resolution.

3d. Heating system balancing

The board noted that balancing is included in the routine maintenance contract and needs no separate resolution.

4. Parking

The treasurer, Mrs. Králová, reported that the income from the 42 courtyard parking spaces no longer covers the cost of snow clearing, lighting and the barrier maintenance contract. The current monthly fee is EUR 32 per space. She proposed raising it. Mr. Němec moved an amendment to raise the fee to EUR 44.50; the amendment was voted down (2 for, 7 against). The treasurer's original proposal was then voted.

Resolution 3/2026-2: The board ADOPTS an increase of the monthly parking fee to EUR 38 per space, effective from 1 July 2026. The treasurer, Mrs. H. Králová, is responsible for notifying the members and updating the payment orders. Vote: 7 for, 2 against. Adopted.

5. Bicycle shelter

Mr. Beneš, the facilities manager, presented the plan for a covered, lockable bicycle shelter for 30 bicycles next to building 18, requested by members at the annual meeting. The location was agreed with the town's building office, which confirmed that no building permit is needed for a structure of this size.

Resolution 3/2026-3: The board ADOPTS the construction of the bicycle shelter next to building 18, managed by the facilities manager, Mr. T. Beneš. The resolution takes effect on the date of this meeting. Vote: 9 for. Adopted.

6. Other business

Ms. Fialová reported repeated failures of the lift in building 16. The facilities manager will ask the service company for a written report. Several members asked that the courtyard lighting be switched to motion sensors; the facilities manager will price it for the next meeting.

7. Budget summary of the resolutions adopted at this meeting

- Facade insulation (Resolution 3/2026-1): EUR 214,000 from the repair fund and the renovation loan approved in 2025.
- Parking fee (Resolution 3/2026-2): no expenditure; additional income estimated at EUR 3,024 per year.
- Bicycle shelter (Resolution 3/2026-3): the approved budget for the bicycle shelter is EUR 9,400, from the operating reserve. The treasurer confirmed the reserve can cover it.

For information, proposals not adopted at this meeting and therefore carrying no budget: heat pumps (voted down), photovoltaic panels (deferred).

The meeting closed at 21:05. Next meeting: 22 April 2026.
Minutes: M. Říhová. Approved: K. Novotná, chair.
